title: Freight agent commission splits: compare the whole deal
seoTitle: Freight agent commission splits: compare the whole deal
searchIntent: What makes a freight agent commission split fair?
excerpt: Evaluate a freight agent split against back-office support, credit, operating duties, payment timing and the business each party brings.
takeaway: A fair agent split depends on the work, costs and risk each party carries. Compare the commission calculation and support package before deciding that the highest percentage is the best offer.

sections.title: What makes a freight agent commission split fair?
paragraphs: The percentage is only part of the deal. Luis describes an agent relationship as a value exchange: the agent brings sales ability and customer relationships, while the brokerage may provide funding, credit, systems, accounting and operational support.

Two offers with the same split can produce very different working lives. One may let the agent concentrate on customers. The other may leave the agent handling invoicing, collections and shipment problems. Write down those duties before comparing the headline numbers.

sections.title: Define the money being split
paragraphs: Ask whether commission is calculated on gross profit, revenue or another contractually defined amount. Then ask which expenses or adjustments come out before the split, and whether any deductions happen afterward.

For a simple illustration, if a shipment produces $500 of commissionable gross profit, a 60% agent share is $300 and the brokerage share is $200. That $200 still has to support the brokerage’s costs. The example explains the calculation; it is not a recommended split or a promise of profitability.

sections.title: Put a value on the support
paragraphs: Look at who approves customer credit, funds carrier payments, handles billing, follows up on documents and helps resolve problems. Ask what happens when a customer pays late or a claim arises. The answer needs to be in the agreement, not just the recruiting conversation.

An experienced agent bringing a productive book has something different to offer from someone who needs training and a customer-development process. The brokerage’s resources differ too. Those differences help explain why there is no single percentage that fits every relationship.

sections.title: Check whether both sides can sustain the arrangement
paragraphs: Luis argues for leaving enough money in the business to deliver the support agents were promised. His preferred structure reflects his brokerage’s model, rather than an industry-wide rule that another split cannot work.

Before signing, request a sample commission statement, a written description of support and the payment schedule. Compare the complete arrangement and have unclear contract obligations reviewed. A slightly smaller percentage can be worth more if it comes with reliable support and fewer costs of your own.
